<!-- Sent by Height -->

I don't think we should switch `includeNodeModules` to `excludeNodeModules`. It's less flexible that way. For example, I use `includeNodeModules` to only include specific node modules when building a library, rather than needing to list every possible module to exclude. This wouldn't be possible with `excludeNodeModules`. Meanwhile, excluding modules is already possible by setting them to `false` with `includeNodeModules`.

The main feature this PR tries to add is globals; `excludeNodeModules` is just semantics. I'll make another PR with only globals support and no `excludeNodeModules`. My only concern is semantic correctness; when you specify a string value in the `includeNodeModules` object, you would assume that the module would be included (since strings are truthy), but in this case the string means that the module is not bundled.
True. What do you think about using the `alias` field in package.json for this instead of `includeNodeModules`?

See [my comment](https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/issues/4846#issuecomment-654419954). I think it's certainly a good idea but there has to be a secondary method for some use cases to specify globals by target.

issue_context.body:
<!---
Thanks for filing an issue 😄 ! Before you submit, please read the following:

Search open/closed issues before submitting since someone might have asked the same thing before!
-->

# 🙋 feature request

The ability to use `excludeNodeModules` rather than `includeNodeModules` in each target config. Many more people need externals than need to forcibly bundle a specific module, so this seems like something that would semantically make sense.

## 🤔 Expected Behavior

```
{
  "targets": {
    "library": {
      "excludeNodeModules": {
        "react": true,
        "jquery": "$"
      }
    }
  }
}
```
A string value should be treated as the name of a global, while a boolean should be whether to keep the `require` or not (though, in my opinion, a value of `true` should cause an error in a browser build).

The same array syntax as `includeNodeModules` should be allowed, but only for exclusion of modules.

## 😯 Current Behavior

With `includeNodeModules`, not only are globals impossible, the syntax to exclude multiple (but not all) modules is cumbersome in comparison to a single array.

## 💁 Possible Solution

The Parcel source must already have some way to exclude any given node module. To add support for globals, Parcel must dynamically generate a fake dependency, i.e. to make `jquery` map to `$`, Parcel could create an asset with solely `module.exports=$`.

## 🔦 Context

This would fix #3305, which I have a similar use case for. Effectively, I'd like to emulate the behavior of [`parcel-plugin-externals`](https://github.com/FlorianRappl/parcel-plugin-externals).

<!--- Providing context helps us come up with a solution that is most useful in the real world -->
comments: This is effectively the same but is meant to offer some sort of structure for implementation. I also disagree with the idea to use `peerDependencies` because those aren't consistently installed (in my experience) with package managers, which can make development annoying.
What do you think about `"alias": {"jquery": {"global": "$"}}`? That would make sense (aliasing a package to a global variable), but it wouldn't be possible to specify per target.

Suppose you're building an isomorphic package for both the browser and the server. You may want to use `pako` from a CDN in the browser (i.e. using a global) but require directly in the Node.js build. You would need some way to specify globals by target to make that work.

That's a niche use case, but I've personally experienced it in the past. In my opinion, `alias` should be the primary method of doing things, but optimally there should be a way to also specify in each target. Perhaps I'll implement both in my PR. Closing because this particular syntax (`excludeNodeModules`) won't be used.
That makes sense. Maybe alias should also be supported per target?

Target-specific aliases would be incredibly useful for library developers. Unfortunately, I'm not too familiar with the Parcel 2 codebase, so I don't think I'll be able to add target-specific aliasing in the PR but hopefully that could be done in the near future.

> That makes sense. Maybe alias should also be supported per target?

+1 to this. It would be beneficial for developers making a "browser-friendly" UMD bundle (alongside the usual esm and cjs) that maps some deps to globals from a CDN. Rollup [fully supports](https://rollupjs.org/configuration-options/#output-globals) this, and honestly this is tempting me to move to it altogether.

> That's already possible: https://parceljs.org/features/dependency-resolution/#global-aliases

I've already tested this and it does this for all targets, am I correct? What I would like to happen is for just some select targets instead as I also output a main/module, but for some users that rely on a CDN and their globals, I also output a UMD that attaches itself so it is defined in `window`. Obviously without aliasing/externals it becomes a huge bundle since my package is a plugin that relies on two other packages.

review_comments: Is this all that's needed to allow support for globals?
Yes (so theoretically, you could create a resolver plugin that does this - without any changes to Parcel itself).

Alright. I thought adding globals support as a core feature would be useful, which is why I made this PR, but if it's out of scope for the project I could remove it and make a plugin. Which is preferable?
We are not against more features, but renaming `includeNodeModules` is a rather breaking change.

I was hoping that breaking changes wouldn't be a major annoyance since Parcel v2 is still in beta and not that many people are using it in comparison to v1. If necessary I'll create a plugin, but I don't like the idea of fragmenting similar functionality into separate places, especially when globals should be configurable on a target-by-target basis.
